entities.summary: The history of Lithuania dates back to settlements founded about 10,000 years ago, but the first written record of the name for the country dates back to 1009 AD. Lithuanians, one of the Baltic peoples, later conquered neighbouring lands and established the Grand Duchy of Lithuania in the 13th century. The Grand Duchy was a successful and lasting warrior state. It remained fiercely independent and was one of the last areas of Europe to adopt Christianity. A formidable power, it became the largest state in Europe in the 15th century spread from the Baltic Sea to the Black Sea, through the conquest of large groups of East Slavs who resided in Ruthenia.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Grand Duchy of Lithuania's expansion from the Baltic Sea to the Black Sea in the 15th century led to the conquest of over 1 million East Slavs and established it as a formidable power, shaping regional politics for centuries. Its lasting legacy can be seen in the modern-day borders of several countries.
